draft.title: Scatter graphs and relationships
card: A scatter graph plots two measures for many places. Each place is one dot, placed by its value on each measure.
the dots slope upward. As one measure rises, the other tends to rise too.
the dots slope downward. The two measures move in opposite directions: as one rises, the other tends to fall.
If the dots are scattered with no pattern, there is no relationship. A relationship shows a link, not a cause, because a third factor may affect both measures or the link may be chance.

2.alt: A scatter graph of two measures for 13 places, one dot each. The dots slope upward from left to right: as the first measure rises, the second tends to rise too. This is a positive relationship.

3.alt: A scatter graph of two measures for 13 places, one dot each. The dots slope downward from left to right: as the first measure rises, the second tends to fall. This is a negative relationship.

draft.remember: A scatter graph shows whether two measures have a relationship. It does not show that one causes the other.

a.q: A scatter graph plots data for 30 countries. The dots run downward from left to right. What does this show about the two measures?
opts: One measure causes the other to fall
a.why: Dots that slope downward mean the measures move in opposite directions, which is a negative relationship. A downward slope shows a link only, so saying one measure causes the other goes beyond what the graph shows.
a.clue: Look at the direction the dots slope.

b.q: A scatter graph of 40 Australian towns shows that towns with higher ice cream sales also have more sunburn cases. What can be concluded?
opts: The measures rise together, but this does not prove a cause
Eating more ice cream causes people to get sunburnt
Sunburn cases cause ice cream sales to rise
The graph shows there is no link between the measures
b.why: The dots show a positive relationship, so the measures rise together. A relationship does not prove cause, and a third factor such as hot weather may affect both. Claiming ice cream causes sunburn treats a link as a cause.
b.clue: Could something else, such as the weather, affect both measures?

b.best: The measures rise together, but this does not prove a cause
